WEREDALE HOUSE IN TWO UNIVERSITY NEWSLETTERS, 1974 AND 1976
and one false positive recorded so it is not chased again

Found 2026-09-07 by the accounted sweep of rma-concordia-publications (p_479).
All three items matched on the keyword "Weredale", not "Kanawana": "Kanawana"
occurs ZERO times in each. They are thin and they are recorded as thin.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. THE HAPPENING, LOYOLA COLLEGE, 11 MARCH 1974
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

From a piece on Loyola's Volunteer Bureau and its new "Help-Bank", a register of
people willing to be called on occasionally rather than committing to a regular
placement — the co-ordinator, Lorraine Street, explaining the difference:
"you're dealing with human lives."

  "On-going projects this year include playing with and taking care of retarded
  children at the John Birk Association; TUTORING BOYS FROM THE WEREDALE HOME;
  serving a meal once a month at the Benedict Labre House for men; doing a
  variety of jobs at the Lethbridge Rehabilitation Centre and the Montreal
  Association for the Blind; being someone to talk to for the senior citizens in
  the Griffith McConnel Home. The Volunteer Bureau also arranges for students to
  be big brothers or sisters to children through Family Services."

NOTE WHICH INSTITUTION THIS IS. *The Happening* was LOYOLA COLLEGE's paper, and
this is Loyola's Volunteer Bureau — not Sir George Williams. Loyola and Sir
George merged to form Concordia in 1974, the year of this issue, so the item
sits on the other half of the merger from everything else this project has
gathered about the university connection. Getting that wrong would put a
Weredale placement inside the SGW-YMCA institutional story, where it does not
belong.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. FYI, CONCORDIA UNIVERSITY, VOL. 3 NO. 5, 7 OCTOBER 1976
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

An open letter from the Chancellor to faculty and staff, soliciting for the
Centraide appeal:

  "As you know, this is a united appeal which has replaced such appeals as those
  formerly conducted separately by the Combined Jewish Appeal, the Federation of
  Catholic Charities, and Red Feather. Centraide now raises funds for some 100
  different social agencies in the Montreal region, providing assistance (to
  name only a few) to such groups as Red Cross, Montreal Diet Dispensary,
  WEREDALE HOUSE, University Settlement, and Y.W.C.A. ... Our objective this
  year at Concordia is to raise $20,000."

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. FYI, 23 JANUARY 1975 — A FALSE POSITIVE, RECORDED AS ONE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The match is "St. Stephen's Church Hall, 1B WEREDALE RD." in a listing for the
Arcadians Musical Theatre Society's production of *The Boy Friend*. Weredale
Road in Westmount is the street the institution was named for — the Boys' Home
of Montreal built on Weredale Park in 1930 — but this is an address, not the
institution, and nothing in the item concerns Weredale House or its camp.

Written down so that a later sweep hitting the same string does not spend the
same half hour on it.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT THESE ARE WORTH
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Small, and honestly two dated data points about Weredale House rather than about
its camp. What they give:

(a) Weredale House was taking university student volunteers as tutors by March
    1974, through an organised college bureau with a named co-ordinator, in a
    list of placements that shows the kind of agency it was grouped with —
    disability services, a men's shelter, a rehabilitation centre, a seniors'
    home.

(b) It was one of "some 100" Centraide agencies in October 1976, named by a
    university chancellor among five examples chosen to stand for the whole
    appeal — so a recognisable Montreal institution to a general readership,
    ONE YEAR BEFORE the 1977 merger into Youth Horizons that
    wiki/connections/related-camps/camp-weredale.md records.

NEITHER TOUCHES THE OPEN QUESTION THE WEREDALE ARTICLE ACTUALLY HAS, which is
whether there were connections between Weredale House and the MONTREAL YMCA
beyond the 1977-1980 two-site planning documents. These are university
connections, on a different axis, and one of them is Loyola's rather than Sir
George's. Said plainly so the addition is not mistaken for an answer.
